skill.name: n8n
skill.description: Create n8n workflow plans and API usage guidance for webhooks, nodes, connections, expressions, REST operations, and MCP integration.

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are explained by Markdown examples in SKILL.md, including fenced JSON and bash snippets, n8n expression syntax, placeholder URLs, and $N8N_API_KEY references. I found no evidence of embedded secrets, prompt injection, unauthorized exfiltration, or hidden code execution. The skill is instructional, but state-changing API examples should remain clearly labeled and require user-controlled credentials.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger command, URL, and secret scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as documentation only and keep placeholder hosts, workflow IDs, and credentials clearly synthetic.

remediation.issue: REST API examples include state-changing workflow operations.
remediation.suggestion: Add a review step before create, update, activate, or deactivate requests, including host, workflow ID, and credential scope checks.

content.value_statement: n8n users need consistent workflow designs and API patterns. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan workflows, webhooks, nodes, REST calls, and MCP integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains core n8n workflow, node, connection, and settings structures.
Provides webhook, HTTP request, IF, Split In Batches, and response node patterns.
Shows REST API operations for listing, creating, updating, activating, and deactivating workflows.
Describes n8n expression syntax for reading item data and node outputs.
Outlines MCP exposure through n8n workflow settings and endpoint access.
limitations: Does not connect to an n8n instance or verify live workflow execution by itself.
Requires user-provided host details, workflow IDs, credentials, and deployment policies.
Examples use placeholders and may need updates for specific n8n versions or custom nodes.
Does not replace review of sensitive data handling, credential scopes, or production change controls.

use_cases.title: Design Webhook Automations
use_cases.description: Create webhook-driven workflows with response nodes, validation branches, and test paths.

use_cases.title: Manage Workflow Lifecycle
use_cases.description: Plan safe REST API operations for listing, updating, activating, and reviewing workflows.

use_cases.title: Expose MCP Tools
use_cases.description: Prepare selected n8n workflows for MCP access with clear boundaries and credential handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an n8n workflow for [task]. Include trigger, main nodes, connections, and test steps. Use placeholders for credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Add API Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this n8n workflow with an HTTP Request node for [service]. Include authentication type, request body plan, and error handling notes.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Workflows by API
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan n8n REST API operations to list, update, activate, and review executions for workflow [id]. Include safeguards before state changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare MCP Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this n8n workflow for MCP exposure. Identify tool boundaries, input validation, credential handling, and safe response design.

output_examples.input: Create a webhook workflow that validates support ticket events and returns a response.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow plan with a Webhook trigger, validation branch, response node, connection map, and testing checklist.

output_examples.input: Show how to manage workflow 42 through the n8n REST API.
output: A sequence for listing the workflow, checking current status, applying updates, and reviewing executions.
Safety notes for API key scope, target host, and activation confirmation.

output_examples.input: Prepare an MCP-ready n8n workflow for an internal lookup tool.
output_examples.output: Guidance on enabling MCP availability, defining inputs, limiting returned fields, and checking credential boundaries.

best_practices: Use n8n credentials for secrets and keep API keys out of workflow JSON.
Test webhook and REST changes against a non-production n8n instance first.
Add explicit error handling before activating workflows that call external systems.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding production hosts, tokens, or credential IDs in reusable workflow examples.
Activating workflow changes before reviewing node connections and response behavior.
Returning complete inbound webhook payloads when only selected fields are required.

faq.question: Can this skill create complete n8n workflows?
faq.answer: It can draft workflow structures and implementation plans. You still need to import, test, and adjust them in n8n.

faq.question: Does it require an n8n API key?
faq.answer: Only REST API operations need an API key. Store it in your environment or n8n credentials.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it execute API calls automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and plans that users can review before execution.

faq.question: Can it help with MCP integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains enabling n8n workflows for MCP and planning safe tool boundaries.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review credential scope, webhook exposure, input validation, error handling, and rollback steps.
